questions.stem: What is the name of the line that divides the Earth into two equal halves and is the largest circle?
questions.solution: The equator is the line that divides the Earth into two equal halves and is the largest circle because it is positioned midway between the poles and encircles the Earth at its widest point. The Prime Meridian is a line of longitude that divides the Earth into east and west, but it is not the largest circle. The Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle are lines of latitude that mark specific regions but are not the largest circle.

questions.stem: What is the angular distance measured from the center of the Earth called?
questions.solution: Latitude is the angular distance of a point from the equator, measured from the center of the Earth. Longitude is the angular distance from the Prime Meridian, not the center of the Earth.

questions.stem: What is the term used to describe the angular distance of a place north or south of the equator?
questions.solution: Latitude is the term used to describe the angular distance of a place north or south of the equator. Longitude refers to the angular distance east or west of the Prime Meridian, not north or south. Altitude is a measure of height above sea level, and azimuth is a direction measurement, neither of which relate to the north-south position.

questions.stem: If a place is located at 30°N, which direction is it from the equator?
questions.solution: Latitude measures how far a location is north or south of the equator. A latitude of 30°N indicates the place is 30 degrees north of the equator. South, east, and west are not used to describe positions relative to the equator in this context.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the meridians of longitude?
choices: They are all of the same length
They are parallel to each other
questions.solution: Meridians of longitude are semi-circles that converge at the poles. They are not parallel to each other and are not circles. They are not all the same length, as they converge at the poles.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct reason for the use of standard time in a country?
choices: To avoid the use of different time zones
To maintain uniformity of time within the country
To follow the time of the Prime Meridian
questions.solution: Standard time is used to maintain uniformity of time within the territorial limits of a country. This is done by selecting a central meridian as the standard meridian. The option 'To avoid the use of different time zones' is incorrect because countries with large east-west spans may have multiple time zones. 'To follow the time of the Prime Meridian' is incorrect because most countries use their own standard time. 'To create time zones' is also incorrect because time zones are a result of the use of standard time, not the reason for it.

questions.stem: If the time at the Prime Meridian is 10 a.m., what will be the time at a place located 30° west of the Prime Meridian?
questions.solution: The time decreases by 4 minutes for every degree of longitude west of the Prime Meridian. For 30°, the time difference is 30 × 4 = 120 minutes or 2 hours. Subtracting 2 hours from 10 a.m. gives 8:00 a.m. The other options are incorrect because they do not account for the 4-minute rule or subtract the time incorrectly.

questions.stem: Why does the International Date Line not follow the 180° longitude exactly in some places?
choices: To maintain the same day in different regions
To align with the Prime Meridian
questions.solution: The International Date Line deviates from the 180° longitude to avoid crossing large landmasses, which helps prevent confusion in daily life and timekeeping. Maintaining the same day in different regions is not the purpose, as the line is meant to separate different calendar days. Simplifying time calculations is not the main reason, as the line's placement is more about geography than math. Aligning with the Prime Meridian is incorrect because the date line is not connected to that specific line of longitude.
